analysis.title: Williams-Sonoma Inc. (WSM): 3Q26 top-line miss as management increases full-price selling initiatives; freight to increase costs
key_insights: WSM closed down 15% on 11/19 versus the S&P 500 down 2%. GS attributes the move to elevated expectations going in, softer comps, possible consumer elasticity from full-price selling, higher material costs, shipping delays, and the omission of the long-term algorithm from the press release.
3Q26 comp was +5.1% versus GS estimate +6.4% and FactSet consensus +5.6%. Retail comp was +1.5% and e-commerce comp was +6.8%. Furniture drove most of the quarter's strength.

Management cut markdowns on seasonal categories across all banners, mainly Pottery Barn, which cut non-furniture sales. Pottery Barn comp was +1.8%. Management plans fewer markdowns and more full-price selling in 4Q holiday.
Banner comps: West Elm +7.0%, Williams-Sonoma +6.8%, Pottery Barn Children +2.9%, Pottery Barn +1.8%. B2B grew 15% with strength in contract and trade.

Diesel costs are about 20% higher than last quarter and could add $60mn of expense for the full year. WSM absorbed 75 bps of pressure in 3Q, partly offset by supply-chain efficiencies and lapping a shrink accrual.

Shipping delays come from Middle East conflicts, typhoon season, and rail congestion at the Los Angeles and Long Beach ports. Delays could take multiple quarters to resolve, and management is willing to pay extra to expedite deliveries.
FY26 guidance was reiterated and includes the higher costs, with an operating margin of 17.8%-18.2%.

The press release left out the long-term algorithm (mid-to-high single digit revenue growth, mid-to-high teens operating margin). Management said the omission was meant to avoid implying FY27 guidance and that it maintains the long-term targets beyond 2027.
GS estimate changes: FY26 comp +6.3% (from +7.0%), operating margin 18.1% (from 18.2%), EPS $9.54 (from $9.66). FY27 EPS $10.48 and FY28 EPS $11.69, down 3.8% and 4.4%.

GS reiterates Buy and cuts the 12-month price target to $252 from $279. The relative P/E multiples were raised to 120%/130%/140% from 100%/110%/115% to offset a lower market multiple of 17.3x (22.6x prior).

WSM trades at 21.4x NTM P/E versus 3-year and 5-year averages of 19.5x and 15.7x. GS says investors need clarity on the timing and effect of the full-price initiatives and a Pottery Barn comp improvement before turning more constructive.
GS notes FY27 EPS estimates fell 4% against a 15% stock drop.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy and cuts the target to $252 from $279 after a 3Q comp miss. It says the company's fundamentals are unchanged and that the 15% drop outweighs the 4% cut to FY27 EPS.

earnings_insights: WSM 3Q26 reported 11/19: comp +5.1% reported versus GS estimate +6.4% and FactSet consensus +5.6%. Revenue was slightly below expectations.
GS FY26 estimates after the print: EPS $9.54 (was $9.66), comp +6.3% (was +7.0%), operating margin 18.1% (was 18.2%), sales $8,300mn.
GS FY27E EPS $10.48 (was $10.89) and FY28E EPS $11.69 (was $12.23). 4Q26E EPS is $3.33 (was $3.40) and 4Q26E comp is +6.9% (was +7.7%).
Company FY26 guidance reiterated: operating margin 17.8%-18.2%, including higher freight and fuel costs.
Diesel costs are about 20% higher than the prior quarter and could total $60mn of expense for the full year. WSM absorbed 75 bps of pressure in 3Q.
risk_factors: Inconsistent demand trends could keep weighing on comps, with share-of-wallet and pull-forward effects in furniture.
Margins could come under pressure once freight tailwinds end, or if a promotional environment develops.
WSM trades above its historical average P/E at 21.4x NTM versus 19.5x (3-year) and 15.7x (5-year).
Consumers may be price-elastic as WSM shifts to full-price selling.
Higher fuel costs, typhoon season and rail congestion at the Los Angeles and Long Beach ports may delay shipments for several quarters.
geopolitical: Conflicts in the Middle East are cited as one cause of product shipment delays.

tension_points.bull_case: Management says newness, collaborations, product innovation and B2B growth can keep winning share while WSM sells at full price. Furniture, West Elm and Williams-Sonoma comps were strong, and GS says its FY27 EPS cut of 4% is small next to the 15% stock drop.
tension_points.bear_case: Fewer markdowns cut non-furniture sales at Pottery Barn and could expose consumer price elasticity. Costs from fuel and shipping delays are rising, and the stock trades at 21.4x P/E against 19.5x and 15.7x averages.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further comp slowdown, a Pottery Barn comp that does not improve, or margin pressure once freight tailwinds end.

theme_stances.key_argument: The company's fundamental strength is unchanged and the stock fell far more than FY27 estimates.
theme_stances.evidence: our FY27 estimates only decreased -4% vs. the stock's reaction of -15%
